Yes, certainly. In fact, I complete most of my projects this way, using photos with the dimensions marked on them.
I am also very interested in long-term cooperation.
Best regards,
[FREELANCER_NAME_001]

[FREELANCER_NAME_003] you for your offer.
Provided that this suits you, I would rather handle the first project at a fixed price.
Considering the project description, my offer is a fixed $500, with delivery estimated in 4–6 days.
How does that sound?

Could you please confirm a few additional details:
What steel grade should I use for the shaft and the remaining parts?
Do you have a company drawing template, or any particular ČSN/EN ISO requirements?
Some dimensions may require further clarification while I am working, so please remain available to answer questions and provide quick confirmations.

Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001],
Good evening!
Will we be proceeding with the project?
I have very limited availability this week, so if we are going ahead, I would like to begin as soon as possible to stay within the agreed timeline.
Please keep me informed.
Best regards,
[FREELANCER_NAME_001]
Apologies for replying late. Since this will be the first project in our cooperation, would a range of 400USD be acceptable to you for completing it?

The only template I am able to supply is for Autodesk Inventor, although I am unsure whether that will work for you. Otherwise, there are no special preferences; the project only needs to comply with the usual ČSN/EN standards.

Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001],
That is no problem, and I appreciate your response.
Yes, I agree to complete this first project for $400 to begin our cooperation.
Please be aware that certain dimensions or technical points might need clarification during the project. Should anything come up, I will contact you so that we can resolve it promptly and continue making progress.
Assuming everything goes well, I am confident there will also be opportunities for us to cooperate on future projects.
Please send the fixed-price contract, and I will begin immediately.

Regarding any measurements that may be needed, a quick response could be somewhat difficult because the part is kept in our storage. Therefore, a possible delay caused by a late reply from my side is OK.

That is completely fine, and [FREELANCER_NAME_003] you for informing me.
I understand that obtaining certain measurements could take some time. Whenever possible, I will gather my questions and send them all at once to reduce interruptions.
I look forward to working together.
Also, please excuse my limited experience with this website, as this is our first time ever using it.

There is no need to worry, [CLIENT_NAME_001].
Everyone has to begin somewhere. I will help keep the process as straightforward as possible, and you can contact me if you have any questions about the platform.
template from Inventor
Here is an example showing how our drawings are set up.
Please keep me informed about how the project is progressing. Thanks in advance.
Got it, [FREELANCER_NAME_003] you! I will begin work on the project within the next 3–4 hours and provide you with progress updates.

Hi, could you review this part? Is it meant to be manufactured as a single solid component, or as a separate ring with four lugs welded onto it? The photo shows that it is welded to the flange, but I cannot tell whether each lug is welded to the ring or whether the ring and lugs form one piece.

I have now created the assembly. However, some dimensions have not been provided, several others are inconsistent, and the intended installation locations for the two separate parts are still not entirely clear.
I have compiled a list of questions requiring clarification and am awaiting your responses. Once I receive them, I will revise the model and provide a sectional view of the assembly using the dimensions available at that point. Additional corrections might still be necessary afterward.
I look forward to receiving your feedback.

Hi, [FREELANCER_NAME_003] you for the comments. I will try to provide clear replies to everything as soon as I can. Because I am traveling to customers, I expect to respond tomorrow or by Monday at the latest, if that is acceptable.
ok
Hello, I have attempted to clarify all the notes you raised. Hopefully, the information will be helpful. If anything remains missing, please get in touch with me. [FREELANCER_NAME_003] you.

Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001],
All right, I understand. Tomorrow, I will go through everything, apply the required revisions, and create a preliminary drawing for you to review.
Best regards,
[FREELANCER_NAME_001]
Could you please provide the model of the sheet unwinder?

A few aspects of the bushing remain unclear. My understanding is that the three holes are for securing it with screws. At the same time, however, the indicated interference fit appears extremely large: the bushing has an outer diameter of 61.2 mm, whereas the mating part has a 60 mm bore.
The countersinks also seem designed to accommodate the heads of countersunk screws, but that would suggest that the bushing is fitted from the other side. Could you clarify the actual assembly method?
The photos also clearly omit some parts belonging to the complete shaft assembly. As a result, I still cannot fully understand the mechanism's operating principle.

I have included all dimensions obtained up to this point. Please keep in mind that this is only a preview for verifying the final dimensions, not the completed drawing. Kindly measure the indicated dimensions again or confirm that they are correct.
The drawing depicts the shaft assembled in the fully retracted position.
Hi, are you available on Telegram so that we can communicate more quickly?
Could you clarify what you mean in this message?
Sorry, don't have
We will go over it with the maintenance team and then get back to you.
If the unwinder is commercially available, could you tell me its model?
No, not really. It was custom made solely for local purposes.

That matches my understanding as well. At this point, I am waiting for you to verify the dimensions in the PDF I provided and explain the bushing configuration. I still do not fully understand its purpose—does it function as a plain bearing?
Are there any photos of the complete machine that show how the shaft was fitted?
Should I also send the 3D model to you now?
I am uncertain whether I can obtain photos of the machine. However, a 3D file is always appreciated.
In general, I believe the model is essentially finished. As noted previously, the only remaining issue I do not understand is the way the bushing must be secured. What file format would you prefer?
Ideally, please provide .ipt, or at least .stp. [FREELANCER_NAME_003] you.
In the meantime, I will produce the drawings for each individual part and await your response concerning the bushing and dimensions.
Do you want the material to be stated on the drawings? If so, please specify the required material for every part.
For the time being, specify standard S355 JRG2 for all parts except the bushing, which should be CuSn12.
ок

Good evening, [CLIENT_NAME_001].
Attached is the first fully completed version of the drawings. Because I still have not received details explaining how the bushing is to be fitted and retained, please disregard its present design. For now, the drawing simply shows it fastened by three screws.
Good afternoon, [CLIENT_NAME_001]. Has everything been clear up to this point? Are there any comments, changes, or further requests from your side? When can I anticipate your feedback?
Hi, I am reviewing it at the moment. Hopefully, I will get back to you today with all the necessary clarification. [FREELANCER_NAME_003] you for being patient.

Hello [FREELANCER_NAME_002],
I have finally managed to inspect everything and review the drawings you provided.

1\. The main difference, which I had not realized before, is that we must produce premachined parts, weld them together, and carry out the final machining afterward. This applies to POS 1+2+3.

2\. The raw input material for the main shaft is tube 108/28, which will be premachined to provide the locations for POS 2+3.

3\. The previously unclear bushing is installed inside the main shaft. **IMPORTANT**: my notes state this incorrectly—the bushing is not fitted to POS 4 and belongs only in the main shaft. Please select an appropriate clearance between the bushing and shaft.

4\. POS 4 carries the piston/rod end together with the nut. The rod from the control piston, which provides the sliding movement, runs inside the main shaft. This is why the inner dia of 55mm must also be machined following welding.

5\. Cross section C-C on the mainshaft drw. shows that this keyway is to be omitted. Instead, the thread for the M100x2 locking nut needs to be wider, and the space for the main bushing must also be wider (40mm).

6\. Where possible, please number the drawings according to the numbering shown on the assembly.

Please update me on the progress, and [FREELANCER_NAME_003] you!
The bushing configuration now makes sense. There is still one question, though: are you certain its length is correct? Relative to the machined seat within the shaft, the bushing appears quite short.
Just to confirm, should these lugs lie in the same plane? They look offset in the photos, so I thought the offset was intentional.

No. As stated in the message (it is shown incorrectly in the drawings), the bushing sits inside the main shaft, and the rod from the control piston is guided through this bushing. Therefore, you need to select a suitable clearance, such as H8/h9, between the bushing and the inner diameter of the shaft. The sliding part contains only the end of the piston.
The angle between the hole axes is 45 degrees, matching both the picture and your assembly.
I think I may be misunderstanding this again. If the bushing is installed only inside the main shaft, does that mean it no longer has to be secured by screws?
With a clearance fit, wouldn’t the bushing remain loose and move inside the shaft? Or is it rigidly mounted on the piston rod?

Since face 1 is flat, I do not believe it needs a machining allowance. Once welded, this face could not be machined on a lathe and still remain flat. We could, however, add a machining allowance to face 2. Another option would be to leave an allowance on face 1 too, then mill it flat after welding. What is your opinion?

I was informed that this bushing is located only in the shaft. However, I am considering another possible arrangement: the bushing would also be secured at the sliding end with the rod nut through it, while the bushing itself would slide inside the main shaft, using its outside diameter as the contact surface. Please prepare it this way. After the drawings are finalized, I will show them to the maintanence manager, and perhaps he will suggest another idea. For now, please proceed like this.
At this point, should the holes be deleted from the bushing, or should they remain in both the bushing and the sliding mandrel?

You are correct: surface 1 should not be machined after welding.
The same applies to surface 2, because machining it would be very difficult. Both surfaces therefore need to be finished before they are welded onto the shaft. Is that acceptable?
Please leave them unchanged.
ок
Do you want the 4 mm groove removed?
That is a good question. I believe there should still be a small groove separating the thread from the bearing surface, though it could perhaps be smaller.
Okay, I’ll prepare the second version and send it for approval either later tonight or tomorrow.
Perfect, [FREELANCER_NAME_003] you
The final choice is 1,6 with the given tolerance field. There was some discussion about it, but 1,6 is the final decision.
👌 I’ll have V2 sent to you within 5 minutes.
That is not a problem. A complete set of drawings would be best, and I will review it tomorrow.
I have included two files containing the same drawings: one is the color version, while the other is the standard black-and-white version. I’ll wait for your feedback :)
Hi, are there any other projects available at the moment? I have some free capacity and could work on them in parallel :)

Hi, apologies for replying late. I’m away on a business trip for a few days. I will probably review your drawings tonight.
If everything is fine and I have no additional comments, I will release the payment.
Would that be OK for you?
Also, if the production manager provides any notes later, would you be willing to update the drawings even after we “close” this project?
We do have other projects, but I first need to prepare everything for you; after that, we can look through it.

From the quick check I can do on my phone, it appears that the groove for the keyway is probably missing from the sliding mandrel part.
As I mentioned, I will inspect everything else later.
[FREELANCER_NAME_003] you.

Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001], yes, that arrangement is fine. I’ll wait until you send your feedback. If any corrections are required, simply message me—I’m available almost all the time. We’ll complete the project and correct everything necessary.
Yes, that keyway is indeed missing :) I’ll put it in.
I’ll wait until you have sent all your comments together. That way, I can apply every correction at once instead of saving the files multiple times.

Good evening,
I’ve reviewed the drawings. Honestly, the version without colours is easier to read. The 3D views could perhaps remain coloured, but every other view should be without colours.
Only very minor corrections are needed; please refer to the notes added to the drawings.

Once this project is finalized, could you provide dwg/dxf files in addition to the pdf files, if possible?
Also, will the 3D files be supplied only as step files? Is there any possibility of receiving a “live format” such as .ipt and .idw?

[FREELANCER_NAME_003] you for making the updates.

Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001], certainly. Exporting the drawings as DWG/DXF will not be a problem.
For the 3D models, I will provide STEP files together with the original editable SolidWorks formats: SLDPRT, SLDASM and SLDDRW. Besides STEP, I can also export the models in SAT, IGES or IFC formats.

Adding this dimension would repeat the overall dimension, which is already given with minimum and maximum values representing the complete travel. Should the existing overall dimension remain, or should I delete it and use the dimension you marked instead?

The overall length can remain, but the functional dimension is the distance between those holes. Please add that dimension, and perhaps place the overall dimension in bracket.
First, please send the final drawing set in pdf. I will confirm it, and you can then export the other formats.
For the required formats: PDF+DWG and STEP+ editable solidworks 3D files and drawings.
ok

Hi,
[FREELANCER_NAME_003] you for sending the final revision. Honestly, the drawings look quite good. As mentioned before, if any further small changes arise, would you still be willing to make them after we close this project?
You may also release all the files as previously agreed.
[FREELANCER_NAME_003] you.

Yes, certainly. I’m available almost all the time, and I also look forward to collaborating with you on future projects.
If any minor adjustments are required, just send me a message and I’ll make them quickly.
The payment has been released; hopefully it reaches you soon.
I just noticed that two reference dimensions on the shaft blank were no longer associated correctly. I have now fixed them.
These are standard 3D formats.
